questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1) I had been on exchange in Barcelona on my bachelors, so I wanted to do a bigger trip. As the exchange selection, first sort away second time exchange students, I had a limited amount of options.

2) Hong Kong had both great academic opportunities, aswell as great nearby travel options. You can both go south and enjoy the beach, or travel around China.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The level at CUHK differs quite a lot, there are both courses were the level is low compared to KU, and courses where KU seems way behind. It can mostly be summoned like this:

1) All courses involve continuous grading, meaning that in almost all courses midterms, assignment, attendence and final exam all count towards the grade. 

2) All courses that involve some kind of presentation or report do, have overall seemed very minimal workload wise. Since most of the local students do not seem very trained in presenting projects, most exchange students have quite an advantage here.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, just email either the Danish or the local guides.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not that much, I had a family friend pick me up in the airport.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is dorm rooms for exchange students (only undergraduate), but only maybe for masters students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a kitchen (not nice), but there is like 20 different canteens and restaurants at the university with good prices.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is not that nice, and you typically share one room with either 1 or 2 other people. However, it is very cheap, as we paid around 8000 HKD (6000 DKK) for the whole semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a long add-drop period, but be quick at applying for pre-approval at UCHP. I had some trouble since they are super slow.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1) Pre apply for courses a few months before.
2) In the first few days you officially apply for courses
3) Courses start, and there is a 2 week add/drop period.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In step 2) there is a meeting with a academic advisor who do everything for you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a bit of both worlds. As the UCPH does not want to approve quite a lot of courses, I ended up with quite a few different ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take the living situation at the college, and look at courses early. You are allowed to take courses from all  faculties. Also check out the examination, it is very nice to have courses that does not have attendence. Since some of the professors are quite difficult to undestand.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have had both the easiest and the hardest course of my 5 years at uni here, so that is quite fun.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I am a second year masters student at the economics department, however CUHK economics department does not allow exchange student. BUT, the BA here is 4 years, so I was allowed to take 4th year courses. I guess then in the eyes of CUHK it is BA courses, and in the eyes of UCPH it is MA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a mix of lectures and tutorial sessions, but not that different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Bayesian Learning: A course about bayesian statistics, from the 4th year at Statistics Department.
Advanced Macro: Only take this course if you are a BA student, I think you can get merit for Macro III. But it is boring as hell.
Investment Analysis and Portfolio management: This course is extremely easy.
Economics of Derivatives: This course is all good if you have had any kind of theorical finance before.
Independet research seminar: I wrote a seminar about Expected Goals models in the Premier League, and compared which algorithm was optimal, aswell as who over/under performed.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you want to learn, and have a challenge,  take Bayesian Learning, I think I used 80% of my reading time on this course. The other courses I would not apply for, from a academic point of view. The research project was nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are loads of football, tennis, volleyball etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Play the football aswell as tennis.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel travel travel. Go explore the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, as there is loads of exchange students here.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go to the classes and talk to them, that is the most natural.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: If you order water, you get a glass of hot water.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food 100p

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Save up for travels.
2) Bring less stuff than you think, it is extremely warm here. Also you can buy stuff only on like 1668/Taobao etc. at extremely cheap prices. 
3) If you play football, there is a danish football team called Hong Kong Vikings, it have been very fun to play there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Yes, look very detailed at the classes before hand, and apply for pre-approval early.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The football team, the friends etc.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference away from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
